common_part.cm4_title: A 10-Year Longitudinal Study of Brain Cortical Thickness in People with First-Episode Psychosis Using Normative Models

cm6_clarity_of_research_objectives.reason: The introduction clearly states the main goal and predictions of the study, which are to map the associations between brain cortical abnormalities and clinical symptoms over a long-term period and to test specific hypotheses regarding these associations.
cm6_clarity_of_research_objectives.supporting_text: Our main goal in this study was to map the associations between brain cortical abnormalities and clinical symptoms over the longer term. ... we predicted that: (i) we would observe a characteristic yet diffuse pattern of case-control differences in cortical normative deviations, consistent with prior studies and (ii) individual differences in cortical deviations would be coupled to clinical outcome over time.

common_part.cm7_additional_comments: The study's main strength is its long 10-year follow-up period, which is rare. The use of normative modeling with transfer learning to handle multi-scanner data is a key methodological feature that allows for robust longitudinal analysis. The finding that cortical deviations attenuate over time, alongside symptom improvement, challenges the simple neurodegeneration hypothesis of schizophrenia.

nm1_clear_definition_of_target_populatio.reason: The 'Participants' section clearly defines the patient population, including diagnostic criteria (DSM-IV SCID-I for first-episode schizophrenia spectrum), recruitment source, and specific diagnoses included.
nm1_clear_definition_of_target_populatio.supporting_text: Here, patients with a first-episode schizophrenia spectrum diagnosis (SCZ) were consecutively recruited from the catchment-area-based inpatient and outpatient services at Oslo University Hospital and 3 additional hospitals in the larger Oslo area to the prospective study. Psychiatric diagnosis at baseline was established using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders (SCID-I 40 ), and we included a broad range of schizophrenia spectrum diagnoses: schizophrenia ( n = 57, 72% of the final, quality-checked longitudinal sample), schizophreniform disorders ( n = 18, 23%), and schizoaffective ( n = 4, 5%).

nm2_clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_c.reason: The paper specifies inclusion criteria for patients and detailed exclusion criteria for controls. However, exclusion criteria for the patient group are not explicitly stated. A quality control procedure for imaging data is mentioned, which serves as a form of data-based exclusion.
nm2_clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_c.supporting_text: Psychiatric diagnosis at baseline was established using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders (SCID-I 40 ), and we included a broad range of schizophrenia spectrum diagnoses...Exclusion criteria for healthy CTRL included a history of drug or alcohol abuse or dependency, psychosis, bipolar disorder, or major depressive disorder, or having a first-degree relative diagnosed with a psychotic or bipolar disorder...An automatic quality check procedure based on the Freesurfer Euler characteristic was run on all data and samples with a value higher than 5 were removed.
nm2_clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_c.location: Berthet2025.pdf.md: Methods / Participants / Paragraph 1 & Methods / MRI Data Acquisition and Analysis / Paragraph 2

nm3_handling_of_confounding_variables.reason: The normative modeling approach (Hierarchical Bayesian Regression) explicitly modeled and adjusted for key confounding variables including age, sex, and scanner site.
nm3_handling_of_confounding_variables.supporting_text: we used the Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) approach for normative modeling, which efficiently accommodates inter-site variation...We estimated a normative model for each region of interest (ROI, n = 150) in the Freesurfer Destrieux atlas, using HBR with age as a covariate, and sex and scanner id as batch effects, to predict CT.

nm4_clarity_of_data_sources.reason: The paper clearly identifies the source of the primary longitudinal dataset (TOP study) and also mentions that the reference normative model was trained on a large collection of mostly publicly available datasets.
nm4_clarity_of_data_sources.supporting_text: All participants were recruited to a specific first-episode sub-study of the TOP study at the University of Oslo and Oslo University Hospital...Using pooled data from a collection of mostly publicly available datasets from 77 sites, and 40 435 participants, the reference normative models were first trained...

nm6_details_of_data_preprocessing.reason: The data preprocessing pipeline is clearly described, specifying the software used (Freesurfer v5.3), the anatomical atlas for parcellation (Destrieux), and the quality control procedure applied (Euler characteristic).
nm6_details_of_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: T1-weighted structural MRI scans were preprocessed through Freesurfer (version 5.3), and CT measures were parcellated using the Destrieux atlas. An automatic quality check procedure based on the Freesurfer Euler characteristic was run on all data and samples with a value higher than 5 were removed.
nm6_details_of_data_preprocessing.location: Berthet2025.pdf.md: Methods / MRI Data Acquisition and Analysis / Paragraph 2

nm7_clarity_of_data_partitioning_methods.reason: The paper describes a clear process for how data were used: a large external dataset was partitioned into training (95%) and validation (5%) for the reference model, and then local control data was used to adapt the model before testing it on the longitudinal study sample.
nm7_clarity_of_data_partitioning_methods.supporting_text: ...the reference normative models were first trained on (95%) healthy individuals and validated on an independent set of 2548 CTRL and patients (5%, stratified by sites). We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners...For this adaptation step, we used held-out cross- sectional data from CTRL from these 3 scanners...After this transfer step, we tested the normative models on the remaining longitudinal CTRL and SCZ samples...

nm8_details_of_normative_modeling_approa.reason: The paper clearly states the statistical approach used for normative modeling, which is Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR), and specifies the covariates (age) and batch effects (sex, scanner id) included in the model.
nm8_details_of_normative_modeling_approa.supporting_text: To account for site and scanner effects, we used the Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) approach for normative modeling...We estimated a normative model for each region of interest (ROI, n = 150) in the Freesurfer Destrieux atlas, using HBR with age as a covariate, and sex and scanner id as batch effects, to predict CT.

nm9_details_of_training_algorithm.reason: The paper identifies the modeling approach as Hierarchical Bayesian Regression and mentions transfer learning with informed priors. However, it does not provide specific details on the optimization algorithms, hyperparameter settings, or convergence criteria, instead referring to previous publications for the detailed methodology.
nm9_details_of_training_algorithm.supporting_text: we used the Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) approach for normative modeling...We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners, by transferring the (hyper) parameters as informed priors for these new sites. For this adaptation step, we used held-out cross- sectional data from CTRL from these 3 scanners, following methods described previously 55...

nm10_model_performance_evaluation_metric.reason: The paper does not report standard performance metrics (e.g., MSLL, R², correlation) for the normative model itself. The evaluation of the model's output is done through downstream statistical analysis of the deviation scores, and a threshold for 'extreme deviation' is defined, but the model's predictive performance is not explicitly quantified.
nm10_model_performance_evaluation_metric.supporting_text: We defined the threshold for extreme deviation values as | z | > 2.0. While this threshold is arbitrary, we consider 2 standard deviations from the mean a potentially clinically significant effect.

nm11_implementation_of_internal_validati.reason: The paper states that the reference normative models were trained on 95% of the large-scale dataset and then validated on a separate, independent 5% of that data, which constitutes internal validation.
nm11_implementation_of_internal_validati.supporting_text: ...the reference normative models were first trained on (95%) healthy individuals and validated on an independent set of 2548 CTRL and patients (5%, stratified by sites).

nm12_external_data_validation.reason: The core of the study involves applying a normative model, which was trained on large external datasets, to a completely independent longitudinal cohort (the TOP study). This process serves as a form of external validation, demonstrating the model's applicability to new data from different scanners.

nm15_interpretation_specific_to_normativ.reason: The discussion section provides a clear and specific interpretation of the findings in the context of normative modeling. It explains how the attenuation of deviation scores over time challenges the traditional neurodegenerative model of schizophrenia.
nm15_interpretation_specific_to_normativ.supporting_text: These findings are in line with previous reports that the gray matter differences were most severe in the early years after schizophrenia onset, and are discordant with a general notion of schizophrenia as a neurodegenerative disorder with progressive brain aberrations over time.
